item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight for SCP (a.k.a The Golden Opportunity)
item.content:encoded:
If this was being done as more of a parody, I could see it. But you would need to have the kid shaken not suicidal, and maybe if the kid was a little older.

The problem is that Wonka is being presented as someone who is super freaky and creepy from the get-go, and that sets off a lot of alarms. Because the kid is being taken against his will and something is done to him that makes him suicidal, it just feels sort of cheap. If the victims weren't so young and you weren't presenting Wonka as "super-freaky" there would be less of a problem.

However, if you were presenting Wonka as more "over-zealous" and with some sort of agenda and the kid was not only older but was more of an evil kid after the experience, you may have something. Especially if the kid was more about manipulation than violence.

You just need to throw some sort of twist related to Wonka rather than just abusing some poor kid. While I don't mind seeing kids killed in horror (I blame 1980s horror movies!), my limit is seeing them hurt this specific way.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight for SCP (a.k.a The Golden Opportunity)
item.content:encoded:
There have been issues brought to me about copyright and trash. It is possible to switch the character name.

I'm pretty certain that just swapping out names wouldn't properly address the fact that you're still just making an overly grimdark, edgy version of Willy Wonka and his Chocolate Factory.

I'll be honest, I personally would recommend scrapping this. Not only does the core premise rely heavily on existing copyrighted work, there are also a lot of gratuitous horror elements added in seemingly just to follow said copyrighted work. I myself as a reader would downvote pretty immediately for this:

Even though Willy is super freaky and creepy, at first the child is not frightened. But when they end up back at the house, they suffer from major PTSD until they either die of stress, malnourishment, or suicide.

It seems incredibly tasteless to write about an entity preying exclusively on children, including abducting them in a traumatic process, and causing their death. Suicide and child abuse are already difficult to write tactfully; the way these plot elements have been handled currently does not convince me that the piece would be workable no matter how many edits you make to it.

I highly recommend that you write something else.

item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
Special Containment Procedures: SCP-5459 is to be kept in a 5x5 meter box at all times. No one is to enter the box unless a controlled testing is taking place. 2 armed guards are to be stationed around the box and containment area, rotating every 20 hours. Anyone who is tested, or has been within 20m of SCP-5459 has to undergo a psych brief and debrief, and a day quarantine. SCP-5459 is able to enter others' minds and cause intense emotional distress if in an enraged state. SCP-5459 is agitated and enraged if more than 3 people are in his box. He will stay in normal form if calm, and if enraged may attempt to telepathically confuse others to get himself out or to harm others. Anyone who's mind has been entered by SCP-5459 are to be quarantined for seven (7) days.1 In the event of a containment breach, all personnel are advised to not approach within 20m of SCP-5459 to avoid getting controlled or enraging SCP-5459. If SCP-5459 is needed to be approached, a *maximum* of 2 personnel may approach. Any Class-D attempting to approach SCP-5459 in a containment breach must be terminated.

Description: [IN PROGRESS], summarily deleted at -17 for being an unfinished work, TSATPWTCOTTTADC and Jacob Conwell witnessing via deletion vote.

Salutations. Long time, first time. I plan to read and possibly vote and offer feedback. I've been away from this site for a while. When I came back, there was a Series 6! item.title: Re: Collapsible and ACS bar not working in sanbox?
item.content:encoded:
The ACS module needs a closing brace after its list of parameters. You need to add a "]]" after the last parameter.

The collapsible needs a closing tag after the stuff that you want to be inside the collapsible - "[[/collapsible]]". You have the opening tag ("[[collapsible]]"), but wikidot doesn't know where you want it to end.

item.title: New SCP Ideas (Scylla & Charybdis)
item.content:encoded:
SCPs based off of Scylla and Charybdis from the Odyssey, and Scylla always breaches containment to get to her sister (Charybdis) in order to join her for what they call "The Great Hunt". In Scylla's Document in one of the addendums it mentions of a cross testing with SCP-914 to create a tranquilizing gas that'll make containing Scylla easier. Now for Charybdis, she is too massive to contain, so she is constantly being surveyed by the Foundation in many locations she has been sighted in. Mainly the Straight of Messina. In order to prevent any more casualties, Scylla and Charybdis must never be reunited with each other ever again no matter the cost.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Articles

Elevator Pitch: Documents for newly discovered SCPs that are a threat to humankind.

Central Narrative: Two SCPs that resemble two infamous Greek monsters from the Odyssey and are running around in modern day.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Whenever Charybdis “calls out” to Scylla, Scylla breaches containment just so she can locate and find her sister so the two can go on “The Great Hunt”, as what one of Scylla’s heads exclaimed. From Scylla and Charybdis’ nature, the Foundation decided to keep the two sort from each other as much as possible.

Additional Notes: I would like feedback on containment procedures and tone.

Central Narrative: A metal box, (width: 8 cm, height: 5cm, length: 8cm) that randomly announces the name of a random person that didn't exist until their name was announced, these people will be called SCP-XXXX-1, 2, etc. If a human touches this box, it will say their full name, then proceed to sound a 60 second countdown. item.title: Seeking greenlight for SCP (a.k.a The Golden Opportunity)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror-ish (I guess)

Page Layout (Optional): Basic components, SCP Classification, a picture or two, containment procedures, description, possibly some test logs.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a golden ticket found in the woods. When a child picks up the ticket, it summons a decrepit and grotesque entity similar to that of Willy Wonka.

Central Narrative: Basically a Willy Wonka who lives in a factory and is summoned by a golden ticket. Small, grey, misformed figures wander around the factory with hoods. They become extremely hostile when in contact with adults. When a child is near, they express a great desire for them to meet Mr. Wonka.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Willy Wonka entity takes the child with the ticket out of the woods, and brings the kid to his factory. They enter, (and if the kid is being tracked, the signal is lost.) They are gone a day until the next morning when the child is returned to the place where they sleep. (Room, basement, bridge, etc.) Even though Willy is super freaky and creepy, at first the child is not frightened. But when they end up back at the house, they suffer from major PTSD until they either die of stress, malnourishment, or suicide. And a box of 12 pack "Augustus Flavored Chocolate" Wonka bars arrive at the sleeping place as well. (With real human DNA to that of the actor of Augustus Glute)

Additional Notes: There have been issues brought to me about copyright and trash. It is possible to switch the character name.

item.title: Re: SCP D and D campaign
item.content:encoded:
I've been thinking about this too, and I think the GOC might actually be a better group for the party to be a member of than the Foundation. It seems like the GOC employs magic-users, arcane and divine, more than the Foundation does, and they're also more focused on combating and destroying anomalies than capturing them, as are most D&D parties. There's not much fun about Nine-Tailed Fox sweeping up after a breach or the Mole Rats getting picked off in another endless underground tunnel, but a GOC party can just roll up and start killing shit.

For extra fun, set it in an SCP-5000 scenario, where the Foundation has gone crazy and evil and is spewing rampaging, highly killable anomalies all over the place. Defend Ganzir, try to protect civilian populations, destroy Foundation Sites, team up with the CotBG, or even try to retrieve SCP-055 and bring it to SCP-579, assuming that Pietro Wilson failed in this timeline.

item.title: Re: The Mother of Meteorites
item.content:encoded:
Ooh, I forgot about the moon base. Great idea! Now all they have to do is move any recovered eggs to Lunar Area-32 before they hatch, and the adults will return to the moon to lay their eggs. Unless, as you said, they need Earth conditions to incubate, in which case the moon base will be full of adorable little meteorite egg incubators. Either way, they'll probably keep a few for a while after they hatch to observe their behavior; maybe the emotional punch could be a researcher who's been studying the babies tearfully stepping out onto the lunar surface and convincing the hatchlings to return to space.

Extra cute option: due to the Moon's nonexistent atmosphere and low gravity, the mother no longer burns up on reentry and can slow down enough to survive the impact, so she can return multiple times to entrust her eggs to the same researchers who took care of her when she was a baby.

Tragic/Aesop/still-kinda-cute option: to emphasize sea turtle parallels, mention instances that have been harmed by collisions with or ingestion of human-generated space junk in Earth's orbit. The Foundation might keep some of these injured instances at the moon base indefinitely or until they can be released, just like a real sea turtle sanctuary!

Thanks for the idea about the stromatolites! Those things are cool.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello! After years of being too lazy to join, I finally made an account. Believe it or not, I've actually been a fan of the SCP Wiki since elementary school, probably around fourth grade? I was introduced to it by my sister, who just really liked giving me nightmares. I was instantly hooked though; I have vivid memories of browsing random articles on the school laptops when I probably wasn't supposed to. I've been in love with horror and weird fiction since, and it's honestly a huge influence on who I am today.

Though I've been a fan for awhile now, I recently rediscovered how much I love this website. For the past few days I've been doing NOTHING but reading SCP articles, drawing fanart, writing fanfic, and resisting the urge to annoy my friends by rambling about it. Now I'm really interested in writing my own SCP, and though I'm super nervous, I'm having a ton of fun coming up with ideas.

I'm constantly amazed by the sheer amount of creativity and talent in this community, and I'm thrilled to eventually contribute to it myself. =)

item.title: Re: The Monster that Didn't Exist
item.content:encoded:
Hey again, thanks for the recrit!

+ Open Response +
- Close -

[…]weird to see a Foundation observation site with no means of self-defense[…].

Again, this would be relevant to almost any other article, but this one is somewhat of an exception. The Site (at the time of this tale) is a ramshackle observation facility in the middle of nowhere set up by a couple of Soviet scientists to monitor and study a poorly understood anomaly (not GRU Division "P"). Due to only functioning as observation of a static anomaly which presents no immediate danger to its surrounds (unless one enters it), there would most likely to no weapons stored on-Site (lack of funding/unnecessary)1. Dr Vasiliev himself mentions that they tried sending in soldiers with recording equipment, but they didn't return.
However, even if there were weapons on-Site (and the scientists had basic combat training), they would understand that firing bullets at something that doesn't exist has as much of an effect as sneezing on it, or asking it politely to leave.
There'd probably be security, sure, but it would be far outside the Site to (as I mentioned in my footnote) prevent people from intruding.
I think that's how things would work, correct me if I'm wrong.

Anyway, thanks for the recrit, hope this clarifies some things!

Footnotes
1. Maybe a couple to prevent people from intruding, but even then the weapon supply would be minimal.

item.title: Re: Hospital that heals you on its own.
item.content:encoded:
You have a lot of unique ideas. Even in the well explored field of medical SCPs you have something that I haven’t seen before. However it seems like you have too many ideas. Every line you’re introducing something new and it makes me wonder what this article would actually be about. I’d recommend revising it. I could see an entire article about “a hospital that tries to turn anything into a healthy human” at the same time I could see “a hospital that cures diseases with strange treatments”. It just feels like too much is happening at once in your current pitch with you talking about difficult containment procedures, cross-testing, and a researcher exploiting the SCP all at the same time. I think you should pick some. My recommendation is to focus on how it tries to transform things into people and throw in the containment difficulties. I’m a little biased because those are just my personal favorites but I also think they have the most potential.

item.title: Lock and ___
item.content:encoded:
A locked, indestructible safe with no key that has a dangerous hallucinogenic and transformative effect on those who stay too close for too long.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

I've posted this one before and intended to approach people directly for reviews, but I've been busy and it's been well over two weeks now since the last post so I thought I'd give the forum one last shot! I have made minor alterations due to the feedback I did receive last time (not from an official reviewer but helpful feedback nonetheless).

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Pretty standard SCP article layout, but I’m going to make use of drop-down “click to reveal” sections to help break down the length.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a 1 m3 metal safe that cannot be opened or damaged by any apparent means. It causes auditory hallucinations in those who stand within 15 m of it for more than 3 hours (cumulative) that tempt them to try to open it. Effect is purely proximity-based – object safely observable from a distance. 3 – 72 hours after hallucinations begin, these victims convert into anomalous humanoids with an innate knowledge of SCP-XXXX’s location and resistance to anaesthetic and amnestics. Each of these beings will stick to 1 of 2 distinct behaviour patterns:

  • SCP-XXXX-1 – “Searchers”. Search obsessively for an alleged key to SCP-XXXX when able. Can become frustrated and violent at times. Lucid and capable of conversation, highly manipulative.
  • SCP-XXXX-2 – Animalistic. Repeatedly attempts to open SCP-XXXX by force, overriding any other behavioural drives. Incapable of conversation.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Features an extensive discovery report on the first emergence of the later-named SCP-XXXX-1, leading to discovery of XXXX and XXXX-2. Also features a report on a recurring incident with SCP-XXXX that the Foundation is still studying. References are made several times to a specific named researcher and her hypotheses/findings at several points to help give a connected narrative feel.
Tried to give the article a progressive narrative, in that SCP-XXXX seems relatively simple at first but every new thing we learn makes it seem more and more trouble.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As previously mentioned, progressive nature of the article meant to gradually increase intrigue.

An incident report states that motion sensors within cell are often tripped and cameras deactivated, only for guards to find the cell completely undisturbed and equipment behaving normally again once they get there (incident does not repeat when SCP-XXXX is under constant guard), suggesting perhaps SCP-XXXX is starting to show awareness and more physically active behaviours, or possibly just messing with electrical equipment (still being studied at “time of report”).

Section at end reveals that an SCP-XXXX-1 instance claimed SCP-XXXX’s area of effect would begin expanding, causing the Foundation to regularly test its size, but SCP-XXXX-1 may have been lying and no changes have yet been detected.

Basically, I’m trying to give the sense with both of these parts that this SCP may or may not be a ticking time bomb of sorts.

Additional Notes: As this is my first SCP idea I’m sure it has plenty of issues all over, so please fire away!

item.title: Re: SCP idea: The immortal Cow
item.content:encoded:
*Manifests in answer to PM request*

I have to echo Peppersghost here; this is a soup of concepts with way, way too much going on and nothing holding it together.

That said, I could maybe see the seed of an surreal-horror-comedy scip in "a cow which is not a cow" if you strip away all the cruft and just focus on the idea of something incredibly wrong that seems to want to be a cow for whatever reason- the narrative arc being something like a series of observation logs gradually ratcheting up the subtle creep factor. Never anything blatant, just enough that we get the idea that we probably want it to keep being a cow. Challenge factor would be extremely high, though- could easily go off the rails without rock-solid writing.
